Lives · 1879–1955

Albert Einstein

Science · Germany / United States · 1879–1955

2 min readWhere it is contestedUpdated 19 September 2026
On this pageWhere it is contestedThe definitive biographyReads across to

In 1905 an unknown patent clerk in Bern published four papers that remade physics.

If you keep one line

Four papers from a patent office outweighed every institution of the age. Position is not the same as leverage.

The four 1905 papers were not variations on one idea. One explained the photoelectric effect and helped found quantum theory, another proved the reality of atoms, and another introduced special relativity with its almost unbelievable consequence that energy and mass are the same thing. A decade later his general theory of relativity reimagined gravity itself as the curving of space and time.

Einstein's ideas have been confirmed again and again — by bending starlight, by the GPS satellites that correct for relativistic time, by the detection of gravitational waves a century after he predicted them. He achieved something almost no scientist manages: he became a global symbol of human intellect, his face and wild hair instantly legible everywhere.

He was also a committed pacifist and a refugee from Nazi Germany. He warned about nuclear weapons whose possibility his own equation had revealed.

01Where it is contested

For the physics itself, specialists send you to Abraham Pais's Subtle Is the Lord (1982), which is far more technical and far better on the science. Isaacson is the life; Pais is the work.

02The definitive biography

Einstein: His Life and UniverseWalter Isaacson · 2007

Written after the release of Einstein's personal letters, explaining the physics clearly while drawing a full human portrait — rebel, husband, refugee, sage.

03Reads across to

Marie Curie — the other scientist of 1905 for whom position was not leverage.

Compounding Machines — the counter-case to that entry's thesis: the century's most important papers came from no lab at all.

The Baptism and the Chain — he did not invent the bomb; Kripke used the people who think he did to show how names actually work.

Emmy Noether — general relativity seemed to break energy conservation. Her 1918 theorem showed why it did not, and why conservation laws exist at all.
